findings.detail: This PR made the not-found marker both localised (`t.smartLookup.notFound`, which is `'غير موجود'` in Arabic) and user-editable, but the preview's red-cell test at line 471 is still `String(c) === "Not Found"`. So for every Arabic user, and for anyone who types their own marker (`-`, `N/A`, or empty — all of which the new input invites), the misses render in the ordinary green "matched" style with nothing distinguishing them. The inverse also holds: a legitimately matched value whose text happens to be "Not Found" gets flagged red. The counts in the header stay correct, which is what keeps this out of high — but the per-cell signal, which is how a user finds *which* rows missed in a 50-row preview, silently stops working in one of the two shipped languages. What would raise this: if the same literal were used to drive anything beyond styling.
findings.summary: Preview's not-found highlighting still compares against the literal English "Not Found"

findings.detail: `setResultPreview` at line 181 pushes `result.header ?? []` as row 0, so when `hasHeaders` is false the `resultPreview[0]?.map(...)` at line 458 emits zero `<th>` elements and the `<thead>` holds a single "#" cell above N data columns. Nothing crashes and the rows still render, but the table has no column identification at all and no `<th>` for a screen reader to associate the data cells with — which is the case where headers are most useful, since the user has no header row in the source to remember either.
findings.summary: With "First row is a header" off, the preview table renders a header row containing only "#"

findings.detail: `readGrid` allocates a `{v,t,z}` object for every cell of both entire sheets — for the 40k-row workbooks this repo's e2e suite already exercises (see the note at `services/excelService.ts:123`) that is roughly an order of magnitude more heap than the arrays of primitives the old `getSheetData` path produced, and `resultRows` then holds the whole join in React state for the session. Complexity is still O(n) with a `Map` index, so this is not the freeze-class regression the handbook's rule 2 targets — the tab was already synchronous before. But the incremental `setProgress` calls the old loops made were removed in favour of a 20 → 90 jump, so a large run now shows a bar that sits still for the whole computation, which reads as a hang. What would raise this: an O(n²) shape, or a confirmed OOM on a realistic sheet.
findings.summary: Both sheets are materialised as one object per cell, synchronously, with no progress between 20% and 90%

findings.detail: Now that `handleDownload` reads `resultRows`/`resultHeader` instead of recomputing (the correct fix for TD-043), the result is a snapshot — but nothing clears it when the inputs that produced it change. Toggling "First row is a header", editing "When nothing matches", flipping Smart Match, or picking different return columns all leave `stats` truthy, the stale preview on screen, and the Download button live. A user who edits the not-found marker to `-` and clicks Download gets a file full of "Not Found" with no warning. The preview and the file still agree with each other, which is why this is low rather than a re-run of TD-043 — the inconsistency is between the controls and the result, not between the two outputs. What would raise it: if the preview were paginated or collapsed so the user could not see the stale rows.
findings.summary: Config changes after a run don't invalidate the held result, so Download exports stale rows

findings.detail: `writeSheet` now sets `cell.s` on the header for both export paths, and the commit message and `docs/quality/tech-debt-register.md` (TD-046) both state "Batch ZIP files now get the styled header they never had." They don't. The single-file path goes through `saveWorkbook` → `XLSX_STYLE.writeFile`, which reads `cell.s`; the batch path at line 217 writes with `XLSX.write`, and `xlsx` is aliased to the patched `@e965/xlsx` community build, which has no style writer and discards `s` silently. `eslint.config.js:58-75` documents exactly this split ("use `xlsx-js-style` only to write"), and `DuplicatesTab.tsx:460` / `FileValidationTab.tsx:646` both use `XLSX_STYLE.write` for their in-ZIP buffers. Cosmetic in effect, but it leaves a closed tech-debt entry recording a fix that did not land — which is the failure mode that register exists to prevent.
findings.summary: Batch ZIP export still drops the header styling the commit says it now gets

findings.detail: The spec covers `normalizeKey`, `buildLookup` and `readGrid` thoroughly, but two of the engine's five exports are never called. That matters most for TD-046: the whole fix is `if (!cell) continue` at `utils/lookupEngine.ts:210`, and nothing anywhere asserts it. The e2e fixture's headers are all non-blank, so removing that guard today reintroduces "Cannot read properties of undefined" on the download path with a fully green suite. `formatCell`'s `catch` fallback for an unrenderable format string is likewise unexercised. The commit's own standard — "Reintroducing the one-guard defect fails 2 unit tests and that e2e" — is met for TD-043 and not for TD-046.
findings.summary: `writeSheet` and `formatCell` have no unit coverage — including the TD-046 crash guard

findings.detail: `readGrid(XLSX: any, worksheet: any)`, `formatCell(XLSX: any, …)` and `writeSheet(…): any` mean the compiler cannot catch a typo in `XLSX.utils.encode_cell` or a misuse of the returned worksheet at either call site. Injecting the module rather than importing it is a sound decision here — `App.tsx:6` notes the 515 KB xlsx bundle is deliberately kept out of the eager graph — but a *type-only* import is erased at compile time and costs nothing at runtime, so the injection pattern and full typing are not in tension. `CellInfo.t?: string` is also stringly-typed where SheetJS has a fixed set of codes, which is the discriminant `normalizeKey` and `formatCell` both branch on.
findings.summary: New engine module takes `XLSX: any` and returns `any` from `writeSheet`
